Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Genetically predicted 25(OH)vitamin D concentration had no causal effect on broad depression.
Sentence: "MR analysis revealed no causal effects of 25(OH)vitamin D concentration, either on DS (inverse variance weighted (IVW); b = 0.025, SE = 0.038, p = 0.52) or on BD (IVW; b = 0.020, SE = 0.012, p = 0.10)."
Measured as: broad depression (BD)
Population: 113,769 broad depression cases and 208,811 controls; SUNLIGHT GWAS of 79,366 subjects for 25(OH)D instruments
Intervention: Genetically predicted 25(OH)vitamin D concentration (six SNPs)
Comparator: None (Mendelian randomization)
Design: other primary study
Sample size: 322,280
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D deficiency was associated with higher risk of major depression at 1 year in CKD patients compared with normal vitamin D levels.
Sentence: "Among 17,955 matched pairs, VDD was associated with increased depression risk at 1 year (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.929; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.52-2.448; p < 0.0001)."
Measured as: incidence of major depression within 1 year
Population: CKD patients aged ≥50 years from TriNetX, propensity-matched
Intervention: Vitamin D deficiency (≤20 ng/mL), measured within 3 months of CKD diagnosis
Comparator: Control group with vitamin D ≥30 ng/mL
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 35,910
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed
